headline: Nearly four in five likely Maryland voters oppose new data centres in the state, a university poll finds.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a poll result reported by a TV news site; the statewide question was asked of 370 likely voters.
importance_line: It matters to Maryland voters and state and local leaders weighing data centre projects, since most likely voters expect higher household electricity costs, but it is a single poll and its margin of error is not given in the report read here.
summary: WMAR 2 News reports, citing a University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) poll, that 78% of likely voters oppose new data centres being built in Maryland and 13% support them. Eighty percent expect new data centres to have a mostly negative effect on household electricity costs, and most of those surveyed also expect harm to water and air quality.
notes: ORIGINAL NOT OPENED: the Baltimore Sun page (pool link) gave only a headline and description, so WMAR 2 News is credited as the outlet read in full. Score 5 kept.
